goal: Prove the opt-in Rust cuda-oxide directional steering projection kernel against current-C semantics while keeping SwiGLU blocked on the observed libdevice/NVVM path failure.

covered_behavior: directional_steering_project_kernel one-block-per-row dot-product projection with shared-memory reduction
ds4_gpu_directional_steering_project_tensor shape validation and power-of-two thread selection up to 256
excluded_behavior: runtime graph integration and default CUDA route

rust_owned_in_this_stage: current-C-shaped in-place row projection with SharedArray reduction and synchronization
not_claimed_in_this_stage: runtime graph integration or default CUDA route

swiglu_blocker.attempted_operation: swiglu_kernel using f32::exp() through cuda-oxide libdevice lowering
swiglu_blocker.first_boundary: f32::min and f32::max lowered to unresolved std__intrinsics__minimum_number_nsz_f32 in device IR; finite-value comparison clamps avoid that independent issue.
swiglu_blocker.blocking_boundary: f32::exp() emitted __nv_expf and selected NVVM IR output; cuda_host::ltoir then failed because CUDA 13.2 libNVVM rejected the emitted opaque-pointer function signature.
swiglu_blocker.required_resolution: Repair the cuda-oxide libdevice/NVVM executable path or provide a semantics-preserving supported exponential path before claiming SwiGLU ownership.
